hook: Energy and compute for a whole space station are priced under this dome.
The Charter Authority sits in the densest core on the station.
The arbitration courts of a space city sit behind this portico.
description: The arbitration courts of a space city sit behind this portico. A columned pediment stands on a street of civic frontages in Noordung, beside the Exchange and Charter Hall.

hook: The first thing a visitor sees of Concordia is a zero-g arrival hall.
description: The first thing a visitor sees of Concordia is a zero-g arrival hall. Signs, public structure and docking views greet passengers as they float in from Earth and the Moon.

hook: A spacecraft floats unsupported in a yard much larger than itself.
A timber boardwalk runs out to a glass handrail 342 m up the end wall, 50 m under the sky.
description: A timber boardwalk runs out to a glass handrail 342 m up the forward end wall of Tsiolkovsky (Rotor 1), about 50 m under the artificial sky. The whole city lies below you.

hook: The Arbor interchange: a 108 m platform with screen doors and a train waiting.
The metro runs 45 m overhead so the street underneath stays free.
Ride through the sky and the blue ceiling becomes a lit machine.
description: Ride through the sky and the blue ceiling becomes a lit machine. In the ascender cabin the opposite city hangs overhead and the open interior of the rotor lies beyond.

hook: Lettuce, basil and kale grow in racks under LED rigs, high in the rotor.
description: Lettuce, basil and kale grow in racks under LED rigs, high in the rotor. A visitor gallery looks down on four stages of growth, the nutrient channels and the harvest gantry.

hook: An ordinary street, except the ground curves up and the buildings run on out of sight.
description: An ordinary street, except the ground curves up and the buildings run on out of sight. This is Tsiolkovsky (Rotor 1) at eye height, on a floor that weighs a full 1 g.

hook: Four rotors, a spine, a shipyard and a spaceport on one 21 km axis.
A park stream falls 2.4 m and lands 7 cm off plumb, because the floor under it is turning.
description: A park stream falls 2.4 m into a plunge pool and lands 7 cm off plumb, because the floor under it is turning. Arbor Brook runs 356 m through Arbor Quarter in Tsiolkovsky (Rotor 1).

hook: The whole station in sunlight from 25 km, radiator farms and port against black sky.
The open port from 6 km: spokes, pier rings and the terminal citadel on one frame.
description: The open port from 6 km off axis. Spokes, pier rings and the terminal citadel fill the frame, with the forward cage running back toward the shipyard beyond.

hook: A gap in the shell shows the industrial rotor (Ehricke) turning in open vacuum.
description: A gap in the shell shows the industrial rotor (Ehricke) turning in open vacuum. It is an open truss, 70 to 80 percent vacuum, that stores and processes lunar and asteroid material.

hook: Look through the open forward cage, past the yard ribs, to the ship under construction.
Four propellant spheres sit well clear of the habitat, behind sunshades.
description: Four propellant spheres sit well clear of the habitat, behind sunshades. Two hold hydrogen and two oxygen, with two storable tanks, radiators and transfer lines nearby.

hook: Each radiator panel is 400 by 200 m, and every watt the station uses leaves through them.
A 170 m dish on a lattice tower, with optical links carrying most of the traffic.
An armoured battery guards the forward end against debris with interceptors and a net launcher.
description: An armoured battery guards the forward end against debris. It has a reload magazine, interceptor cells, a net launcher and a Whipple skirt over the housing.

hook: This tethered power platform is where the station's electricity begins.
The power platform on the shade side, lit by Earthlight and a dozen work lamps.
A 22 m metal asteroid in a net bag, pushed home at 37 N over years.
description: A 22 m metal asteroid in a net bag, pushed home at 37 N. The hauler is a 110 m truss with two 60 m solar wings and a thruster plate, and a haul takes years.

hook: Seven Hall thrusters push 30,000 t of asteroid home on about 120 t of propellant.
The aft face from 25 km: red rim lights, a central tower, landing masts and reactor masts.
description: The aft face from 25 km: ribbed, with red rim lights, a central tower, four landing masts carrying marker lights and two reactor masts standing clear of the hull.

hook: Four HVDC landing masts take the power tethers. The station's electricity arrives here.
A black-start reactor sits on an 800 m mast behind a shadow shield.
Twelve Whipple-shielded thruster pods ring the aft face and keep the station on its orbit.
A pressure sphere on the aft tower rim, with the iris, the tower and the stars outside.
Earth is 1.9 degrees across and the Moon half a degree, seen from L5 at true size.
After launch the whole armoured mountain recedes, and passengers see how large home is.
A 10 km electromagnetic track sends passengers away from the station at 1.5 g.
description: A 10 km electromagnetic track sends passengers away from the station at 1.5 g. Gantries line the track along the hull, and the shuttles wait at its start.

hook: An ivory shuttle waits in its bay on the launch track between flights.
Pier P1 on the outer face of the end bulkhead, with a freighter alongside and tugs working.
description: Pier P1 on the outer face of the end bulkhead, with a freighter alongside and tugs working. The axial aperture of the spaceport opens up beyond the pier.

hook: Five cars run the spine at 140 m/s on levitation bogies.
A transit bridge carries people between two rotors, 45 m above the ground and over vacuum.
A 300 m vacuum gap between the rotors exposes their ends, bearings and service lines.
Four bronze blade trusses rise past 800 m with three cab tracks toward the axis.
A grow gallery and a utility plant glow from the open fringe at the 1,000 m service tier.
Six horizontal vessels and two spheres on a lattice deck, in open vacuum at 0.4 g.
A cargo tug hauls a pod slowly along an axial rail in the open outer band.

title: Transfer Station
hook: A 420 m truss in high Earth orbit is where passengers change from the Concordia shuttle to a spaceplane.
description: The 420 m transfer station in high Earth orbit, 950 by 47,527 km. Passengers change here from the Concordia shuttle to a spaceplane bound for the skyhook.

title: Skyhook: Wide View
hook: A 600 km tether turns against the stars and swaps spaceplanes at its two tips.
description: A 600 km rotating tether seen from 1,200 km off. Its tips catch a spaceplane from Earth and release one down to it in a single half-turn, against the stars.

title: Skyhook: Upper Terminal
hook: The upper tip of the skyhook catches a spaceplane in a net of fine strands.
description: The upper terminal of the 600 km skyhook at its 750 km high point, 150 m off. The tether runs down toward Earth, and the capture head waits for a spaceplane.

title: Skyhook: Lower Terminal
hook: The lower tip of the skyhook grabs a spaceplane 150 km up and carries it on.
description: The lower terminal of the skyhook at its 150 km low point, 150 m off, with Earth's limb behind the grapple head that catches and releases spaceplanes.
